fullPassage: When artists represent the human form in works of art, the narratives of culture become embedded in the manner in which the body has been fashioned therein. And while artists may enhance, exaggerate, or take artistic license with that representation to satisfy their client, to make an artistic statement, or to challenge hegemonic norms, the manner in which the body is fashioned in an artwork provides clues to the expression of aesthetic ideals and norms for that period in history. These clues might include the posture, gaze, and stylization of the body of the sitter, the extent to which the figures are dressed or undressed, the types and colors of textiles and embellishments depicted, how the hair is fixed, and what accessories or props are included. As Anne Hollander, a historian of art and dress, expressed in her book Seeing Through Clothes, “clothes make, not the [wo]man, but the image of the [wo]man,” such that art and clothing are “connected links in a creative tradition of imagemaking.”

questions.passage: When artists represent the human form in works of art, the narratives of culture become embedded in the manner in which the body has been __________ (fashion) therein.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 'has been + 과거분사' 형태의 현재완료 수동태이므로 fashion을 fashioned로 바꿔야 한다.
det.analysis: the body has been __________ (fashion) → '신체가 빚어져 온' 이라는 현재완료 수동태(has been + p.p.) → fashion + -ed → fashioned
det.tip: 현재완료 수동태: has been + 과거분사 → fashioned

questions.passage: These clues might include the posture, gaze, and stylization of the body of the sitter, the extent to which the figures are dressed or undressed, the types and colors of textiles and embellishments __________ (depict), how the hair is fixed, and what accessories or props are included.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 명사 textiles and embellishments를 뒤에서 꾸미며 '묘사된'이라는 수동의 의미이므로 과거분사 depicted가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: textiles and embellishments __________ (depict) → 명사를 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사(수동, ~된) → depict + -ed → depicted
det.tip: 명사 후치 수식 과거분사(수동): depict → depicted

questions.passage: When artists represent the human form in works of art, the narratives of culture become embedded in the manner in which the body has been fashioned therein. And while artists may enhance, exaggerate, or take artistic license with that representation to satisfy their client, to make an artistic statement, or __________, the manner in which the body is fashioned in an artwork provides clues to the expression of aesthetic ideals and norms for that period in history. These clues might include the posture, gaze, and stylization of the body of the sitter, the extent to which the figures are dressed or undressed, the types and colors of textiles and embellishments depicted, how the hair is fixed, and what accessories or props are included. As Anne Hollander, a historian of art and dress, expressed in her book Seeing Through Clothes, “clothes make, not the [wo]man, but the image of the [wo]man,” such that art and clothing are “connected links in a creative tradition of imagemaking.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 의뢰인을 만족시키고 예술적 주장을 하는 것과 나란히, 예술가가 표현에 자유를 발휘하는 목적으로 '지배적 규범에 도전하기 위해'가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① to lower the price of their paint — 물감 값을 낮추려고 (예술적 목적과 무관)
❌ ② to hide their own true identity — 자신의 정체를 숨기려고 (문맥 무관)
✅ ③ to challenge hegemonic norms — 지배적 규범에 도전하려고 ←정답
❌ ④ to copy older, famous sculptures — 옛 유명 조각을 베끼려고 (창의적 자유와 상충)
det.tip: satisfy client / make an artistic statement 와 병렬 → to challenge hegemonic norms

ch: to lower the price of their paint
to hide their own true identity

questions.passage: When artists represent the human form in works of art, the narratives of culture become embedded in the manner in which the body has been fashioned therein. And while artists may enhance, exaggerate, or take artistic license with that representation to satisfy their client, to make an artistic statement, or to challenge hegemonic norms, the manner in which the body is fashioned in an artwork provides clues to the expression of aesthetic ideals and norms for that period in history. These clues might include the posture, gaze, and stylization of the body of the sitter, the extent to which the figures are dressed or undressed, the types and colors of textiles and embellishments depicted, how the hair is fixed, and what accessories or props are included. As Anne Hollander, a historian of art and dress, expressed in her book Seeing Through Clothes, “clothes make, not the [wo]man, but the image of the [wo]man,” such that art and clothing are “__________.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 옷이 사람의 이미지를 만든다는 Hollander의 말에 이어, 예술과 옷을 이미지를 만드는 창의적 전통 속에서 '연결된 고리'로 본다는 결론이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① unrelated tools with no shared history — 공유된 역사가 없는 무관한 도구 (연결성과 반대)
❌ ② identical copies of one fixed object — 하나의 고정된 대상의 똑같은 복제품 (창의성과 상충)
❌ ③ temporary trends that soon disappear — 곧 사라지는 일시적 유행 (전통과 상충)
✅ ④ connected links in a creative tradition of imagemaking — 이미지를 만드는 창의적 전통의 연결된 고리 ←정답
det.tip: art and clothing are → connected links in a creative tradition of imagemaking(연결된 고리)

ch: unrelated tools with no shared history
identical copies of one fixed object
connected links in a creative tradition of imagemaking
